title: Library object stories
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

Create a mini exhibition about everyday objects from a fictional neighborhood library's lending collection. The three objects are a 1978 metal recipe box with 46 handwritten cards, a 1996 cassette recorder that belonged to a local bird club, and a 2011 folding shopping trolley repaired twice by its owner. The exhibition sits in a shallow display case for visitors aged 10 and up. Use the objects to invite reflection on reuse and memory, and choose artifacts for both reading and visitor participation. The case has no power and is viewed from one side.

files.body:
# Still in use
### A tabletop exhibition from the fictional Larch Street Library

Allow about three minutes to look and read, plus a minute to leave a memory. All reading and handling take place on the visitor’s side.

## Prepare the paper

Print **Case and station panels.pdf** once, single-sided on matte US Letter stock at actual size. Cut between matching crop marks using a straightedge. Each sheet makes two 7½ × 4⅔-inch panels. The first four panels go inside the case. Page three supplies the two pieces for the visitor station.

Print **Visitor memory cards.pdf** on ordinary uncoated paper at the same settings. Cut four cards per sheet. Start with five sheets for twenty visitors. Gather a pencil, a clipboard, a shallow tray for blanks, a stiff backing board and paper tape for the return pocket.

## Arrange the case

A suggested starting footprint is 48 × 24 inches. Measure the actual objects, the folded trolley and the clearance below the closed lid before placing anything. The sketch looks down from above. The visitor stands along the bottom edge.

```
BACK OF CASE
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Still in use                                          │
│                                                       │
│ Metal box          Cassette recorder    Folded trolley│
│ and cards                                             │
│                                                       │
│ 1978 label         1996 label           2011 label    │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
VISITOR SIDE                              Paper station →
```

Set the introduction on a low wedge facing forward. Give the trolley the widest bay. Lay it folded on a padded support and block its wheels. Turn a visible repair toward the viewer if possible. Keep the recorder flat with its controls facing up. Nest the box on a firm pad. If the lid clears the glass, support it open and show one handwritten card in a separate paper cradle. Keep the remaining cards in order. If clearance is tight, close the box and show the single card beside it.

Place the date labels directly in front of their objects. Check sight lines from a seated position and at a child’s standing height. If space is tight, mount the introduction just outside the left edge. Choose a case long enough for the folded trolley to lie flat, with enough headroom for its thickest part. Keep every object clear of the glass.

## Set out the activity

Use a reachable writing surface just beyond the right end of the case. Set out the activity sign, blanks, clipboard and pencil. Tape the return-pocket panel to its backing along both sides and the bottom, leaving the top open. Slip a folded strip of card inside as a false bottom about an inch above the lower edge so deposited cards protrude. Secure the pocket upright where a visitor can reach it.

To start an empty pocket, write this fictional example on one card and mark it “Example” under the drawing prompt.

> My object: a jam jar.  
> I remember the time we washed out the last spoonful of jam and filled the jar with buttons. The lid still clicks the way it did at breakfast.

Before opening, read each panel through the closed glass. Try drawing on a card, depositing it and picking it out again. During open hours, refill the tray and remove shared cards containing names or private details.

# Still in Use

A tabletop exhibition for ages 10 and up from the fictional Alder Street Library. Three everyday objects show how reuse carries memories forward. Allow about 3–5 minutes for looking, reading, and leaving a lending note.

## Print and cut

Print single-sided on US Letter at **Actual Size / 100%**. On A4, center the pages at 100%. Cut along the crop marks. Use matte cardstock for the display pieces and ordinary uncoated paper for the slips.

| File | Print plan |
| --- | --- |
| [01 Case Panels.pdf](01%20Case%20Panels.pdf) | Print both pages for the title panel and three labels. Each piece is about 176 × 89 mm. |
| [02 Visitor Activity.pdf](02%20Visitor%20Activity.pdf) | Print page 1 once for the activity sign and box label. Print page 2 as needed. Each sheet makes six slips. Start with four sheets for 24 slips. |
| [03 Object Stand-ins.pdf](03%20Object%20Stand-ins.pdf) | Print both pages if you need stand-ins. Each illustration is about 176 × 104 mm. Match its number to the label. |

## Set up from the visitor side

```text
                           BACK OF CASE
                          STILL IN USE

    01 Recipe box     02 Cassette recorder     03 Folded trolley
       Its label           Its label               Its label

                            VISITOR SIDE   →   Activity station
```

1. Measure the usable interior, including the clearance under the lid. Lay out the objects or stand-ins from left to right with the labels along the visitor edge. Place the title panel behind the objects where it stays visible. With the stand-ins, three bays with 12 mm gaps take about 554 mm of width before side margins. Two rows of print pieces take about 205 mm of depth with a 12 mm gap, plus room for the title panel. If space is tight, put the title panel on a stand beside the front left corner.
2. If displaying physical objects, cradle the recipe box and support the lid so visitors can see the cards without disturbing them. Keep the cassette recorder switched off and remove any batteries. Fold the trolley and set it flat with the wheels blocked and the frame supported. Turn a visible repair toward the glass if possible. Use a stand-in for any object that cannot be safely supported within the available clearance.
3. Tilt the labels toward the viewing side as needed. Check them through the closed glass from standing and seated positions, and adjust the angles if reflections obscure the text. Leave an uncut set of the case panels at the activity station for close reading.

## Run the activity

Place the sign, slips, pencils, a firm writing surface, and a closed box with a slot and the **Lending notes** label just outside the visitor edge of the case. Use a surface visitors can reach while seated and keep the viewing route clear. Visitors can write or draw, then drop their slip in the box or take it with them. The display and activity run without power or staff facilitation.

Refill the slips and empty the box at closing. Keep responses private and recycle them at the end of the exhibition.
